claims.rationale: The entire body of the 'from' skill is one instruction: 'Call the Skill tool with "grilling"' (line 7). It adds no procedure of its own, so loading both places one behaviour in context twice. The two differ only in who may trigger them: the 'from' skill's frontmatter sets disable-model-invocation: true and the 'to' skill's does not. That difference is an invocation boundary set by the source and enforced by the harness, not a behavioural one. Both canonical skills keep their identity, history and ownership: this relation records that the two share one behaviour at these pinned bytes, and it is no reason to merge, remove or re-curate either record. The canonical record of the 'from' skill still describes it as a lighter variant with its own procedure; the redirect is what its linked upstream file contains at the pinned commit. This is a reading of the two texts; no run has compared sessions with one against both. Falsified if a session with both loaded follows a procedure that a session with only the 'to' skill does not.
